newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 23.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Greenspan gave no hint that an increase in interest rates is imminent and stocks soared in reaction to the remarks.
* Greenspan's remarks also reassured a nervous bond market and ignited the strongest one-day climb in bond prices since April 29.
* Boeing is close to winning European approval for its $14 billion acquisition of McDonnell Douglas after offering concessions.
* IBM shuffled the jobs of several top executives.
* The U.S. budget gap totaled just $11 billion for the first nine months of this fiscal year.
* Five major drug companies reported higher second-quarteer earnings.
* Philip Morris and RJR Nabisco Holdings posted earnings that met forecasts.
* Britain's BAT Industries agreed to buy the cigarette subsidiary of Mexico's Empresas La Moderna.
* Arthur Andersen named Jim Wadia world wide managing partner of the giant accounting firm.
* Kimco Realty 's chairman plans to split the company.
* Bell Atlantic and NYNEX posted profit gains that slightly topped analysts expactations.
* Walt Disney reported better-than-expected profit for its fiscal third quarter.
* United Airlines' parent posted a 23 percent gain in second quarter net.
* Chase Manhattan appointed Marc Shapiro to the post of vice chairman for finance and risk management.
* Tokyo stocks declined broadly on profit taking.
* J.P. Bryan, CEO of Gulf Canada Resourcs, is ruffling feathers in Canada with his aggressive takeover style.
